ROW.COLUMN: (ML/CB) Pattern of Funds Transfers Between Correspondent Banks

Correspondent banking is considered particularly vulnerable to money laundering activities. Therefore, financial institutions are expected to apply due diligence procedures and effective monitoring to their respondent (correspondent) bank accounts. Understanding the patterns in their respondent bank`s activity with each other helps improve the institution`s knowledge of its customers and identify the potential areas of concern. This scenario identifies patterns of potentially suspicious activity among correspondent bank accounts, such as high levels of activity or activity that indicates the existence of exclusive relationships between correspondent banks.

Primary Rule of this scenario ( based on dataset ML_FTN_ClBnk_Wr_Trans_Actvt ) provides the strongest filtering factor for the pattern to make functioning of next Sub-rules more efficient. It provides Frequency-Period filtering and apply all TSD filters too. The main idea of this dataset is to weed out Client Banks, which haven't showed any activity since the last scenario run. So, only Client Banks, who showed some activity during Frequency Period will be considered during father behavior detection stages.
The next Sub-Rule, based on the ML_FTN_ClBnk_Wr_Trans_Data dataset , provides calculations for all values, needed to realize alert-generation logic in the following Check-Point. In this Sub-Rule we calculate values for highlights and score bindings, conditional thresholds and prepare all data for alert generation logic, realized in the following checkpoint.
The last pair of datasets, following the Check-Point, doesn't take part in behavior-detection logic and just provide supporting data for highlights and augmentation Instructions.
